exec: A maintenance-related disruption to a top-secret government network; critical communications reportedly stayed available.
impact: The agency staggered staff arrivals and logins and sent non-essential staff a Code Gray notice; a source said classified work continued unimpeded.
plain: The classified internal network used by US National Security Agency staff went down or ran intermittently from November 17. The agency cites routine scheduled maintenance; CNN's sources said there was no evidence of a cyberattack.

sources.name: New Turkish Post (Arabic): outage enters third day

summary: CNN reported, citing six people, that NSA Net went down on 17 November; other sources say service was intermittent. The NSA cites degradation during scheduled routine maintenance; DNI Jay Clayton blamed a PHP patch. CNN's sources said there was no evidence of a cyberattack. New Turkish Post, relaying CNN, said on 20 November the outage was in its third day, with repairs slower than expected.
title: NSA's classified internal network NSA Net goes down

validation.note: Agency statement plus several outlets; extent of the outage is described differently by different sources. The Record's second-day report (read) cites one unnamed source for the network working and restoration taking a day or two.

review.note: Compared with The Record (2), WRAL/CNN, New Turkish Post: summary cut under 75 words; no evidence of cyberattack now attributed to CNN sources (Clayton PHP patch cause kept); plain no longer says the agency stated it; day 3 and slower repairs per CNN relayed by New Turkish Post
